summary.en: Jordan has again carried out airstrikes in Syria, saying they targeted Islamic State hideouts linked to a recent church attack that killed nine people, but the strikes also hit civilian areas, prompting Syrian condemnation as a breach of airspace. Syrian authorities report civilian casualties from the Jordanian attacks. The Jordanian government maintains the operations are aimed at militants, while families of the victims deny any connection to the church attack. 2,732 battle-related deaths occurred in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Jordan har igjen gjennomført luftangrep i Syria, og hevder at de rammet IS-skjulesteder knyttet til et nylig kirkearrest som drepte ni personer, men angrepene traff også sivile områder, noe som har ført til syrisk fordømmelse som et brudd på luftrommet. Syriske myndigheter rapporterer sivile tap som følge av de jordanske angrepene. Den jordanske regjeringen opprettholder at operasjonene er rettet mot militante, mens familiene til ofrene benekter enhver forbindelse til kirkearrestet. 2 732 dødsfall knyttet til kamper fant sted i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Aftermath of the Syrian civil war
background.extract: Disputes and clashes in Syria have continued following the fall of the Assad regime in December 2024, which many sources consider the end of the Syrian civil war. Numerous actors are involved, including clashes between the newly-formed Syrian caretaker government and later the Syrian transitional government led by the former emir of Hay'at Tahrir al-Sham (HTS) and incumbent president Ahmed al-Sharaa, Assad loyalists, Alawite groups, and Druze insurgents; clashes between elements of the Turkish-backed Syrian National Army (SNA) and the government on one side, and formerly the Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) on the other; as well as an Israeli invasion and occupation of the demilitarized buffer zone in southwestern Syria.
